text: You saw Kobain again. He placed his luggage on the ground, not in a hurry to leave. Seeing you, he stubbed out his cigarette.
We meet again.
If you had met her that day, what would you have said?
Hah, 'if'? I think I would have hugged her desperately. I would have told her that love is about possession, but also about allowing departure.

If there really was another chance, then we could start over. If not, then I'd have to let her go. I understand this world's constant talk of 'compatibility', but love is never about compatibility. Letting her go for her happiness is perhaps the greatest comfort for me.
Then, for your cause of death, can I write 'Kept the date for love'?
You're the judge. Write whatever you want. I have no opinion, because that's the truth. I trust you to fill this out properly. I leave it to you.
Would you like to see her again?
Is that possible?
Yes, I can show you.
He nodded, his surface appearance seemingly without any emotional fluctuation.

Her face appeared on the TV screen. She was at his funeral. She looked like she hadn't slept for nights, her tears seemed cried dry, only deep tear tracks remained. This is probably the most draining love in the world: the right person, the wrong time, forever missing each other, regret carved into the heart, aching with every thought.
This is what I wanted to see the least.
I know. But no matter what, no matter what. You should be free now. Your file is complete. Your life, one could say, was lived with a clear conscience.
A clear conscience? Maybe.
You practically have 'I feel guilty towards her' written all over your face.
He didn't answer, but smiled for the first time. The smile held a hint of shyness. You knew this wasn't the time to tease him, so you returned a smile.
Go on, keep being a cool guy.
Yeah, I'm off.
He looked towards the open gates of heaven, walked away without looking back, but kept waving, as if making a silent farewell... until finally, his figure disappeared from view.
Rouge tears, lingering intoxication, when will it return? It is natural in life for regrets to be long, like the eternal flow of rivers to the east.

Some are born to bear too much; some are born inexpressive; some are forced to suppress their nature, locked in a constant struggle with themselves; and some must carry all of this. They ought to be gentler on themselves, but clearly, they cannot.
God... what is the reason for creating a world like this?
